assets.name: fire-atlas
assets.prompt: Game VFX production texture. A precise 4 by 4 flipbook sprite atlas, exactly sixteen equally sized square frames arranged in row-major temporal order, on a truly transparent RGBA background. Square 2048x2048 output. Every tile depicts the SAME physically realistic turbulent flame jet flowing HORIZONTALLY LEFT TO RIGHT: white-yellow hot root starts near the left eighth, bright yellow-orange inner fire, rich orange-red thin curling tongues splitting toward the right, small detached embers, wispy semitransparent edges. Not vertical campfires. Real photographed/composited high-speed dragon-breath fire, no dragon, no nozzle or torch. The flame changes naturally from tile to tile as one coherent animation: turbulence and combustion travel left to right, steady output, no beginning/end fade. Each flame stays within its tile with a generous transparent gutter on all sides; repeat exactly aligned root, scale, extent and exposure in all sixteen tiles. Clean sharp fire detail and layered transparency, no rectangular backgrounds, no labels, numbers, grid lines, checkerboard baked into pixels or decorative borders. Not an illustration. This is a technical reusable VFX atlas, not a screenshot or poster.

assets.name: smoke-density
assets.prompt: A seamless tileable grayscale smoke-density texture for a high-quality game VFX shader. Square 1024x1024. Only scalar grey values: black is empty, white is dense, medium-grey turbulent rolling smoke masses. Physically plausible multiscale billows, curling wisps and fine fractal detail, soft organic edges with strong intermediate tonal values. Uniform statistical density across the entire tile, no obvious central puff, no light direction, no three-dimensional scene, no fire, no objects, no text, no colored pixels. Opposite edges must tile seamlessly without hard seams. Crisp usable production noise texture, not a photograph of smoke in a room.
